en: Itivuttaka 96: Tikanipāta, Pañcamavagga (The Fifth Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: “Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a shallow pool with a clear bottom, where one can see the shells, gravel, and pebbles, and where various fish swim about and dwell; this is the first kind of person. The person who is like a deep pool with a turbid bottom, where one cannot see the shells, gravel, and pebbles, nor the various fish swimming about and dwelling therein; this is the second kind of person. The person who is like a deep pool with a clear bottom, where one cannot see the shells, gravel, and pebbles, but where the various fish swim about and dwell; this is the third kind of person. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, a certain monk approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him: “Friend Ānanda, what is the meaning of this that was said by the Blessed One: ‘There are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world’? “It is, friend, because of the three kinds of wisdom that the Blessed One said this. What three? The person who is like a shallow pool with a clear bottom... [as above] ...this is the first kind of person. The person who is like a deep pool with a turbid bottom... [as above] ...this is the second kind of person. The person who is like a deep pool with a clear bottom... [as above] ...this is the third kind of person. It is, friend, because of these three kinds of wisdom that the Blessed One said this. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. And this is the meaning of what was said by the Blessed One, and thus it was understood by the Venerable Ānanda. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard. This was said by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park, concerning a certain monk. At that time, that monk was dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute. Then, as he was reflecting on the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, he attained the destruction of the taints in that very life. Then, when the night had passed, that monk approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, while dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, as I was reflecting on the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, I attained the destruction of the taints in that very life. “Good, good, monk! It is well that you have attained the destruction of the taints in that very life, having reflected on the Dhamma taught by me. For, monk, when a person reflects on the Dhamma taught by the Tathāgata, they will attain the destruction of the taints in that very life, or if not, they will attain final knowledge within seven days, or if not, within six days, five days, four days, three days, two days, or within one day. Or, if not, then within seven nights and days, they will attain final knowledge. But beyond that, monk, there is no further state of being for one who has abandoned birth. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. And this is the meaning of what was said by the Blessed One, and thus it was understood by that monk. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard. This was said by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park, concerning the Venerable Sāriputta. Then, as he was reflecting on the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, he attained the destruction of the taints in that very life. This was said by the Blessed One while staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park
The Discourse on the Bond of Sensual Desire.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, one who is bound by the bond of sensual desire and bound by the bond of existence is a returner, one who comes back to this state of being."
“Monks, one who is detached from the bond of sensual desire but bound by the bond of existence becomes a non-returner, one who does not come back to this state of being.
Monks, one who is detached from the bond of sensual desire and detached from the bond of existence is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed.
Thus the Blessed One spoke on this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
“Bound by the yoke of sensual desire,
and likewise by both the yokes of existence;”
Beings go through saṃsāra,
subject to birth and death;
but those who have abandoned sensual desires—
Not having attained the destruction of the taints,
but bound by the yoke of existence,
they are called non-returners.
But those whose doubts are severed,
for whom conceit and renewed existence are exhausted—
they alone have truly reached the further shore in this world.
"Those who have attained the destruction of the taints.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The seventh [sutta].
The Third Recitation Section.
